stages.name: Independent
stages.desc: Greek Cyrene and the Libyan peoples, outside any empire

stages.name: Persian Empire
stages.desc: Ruled by the Great King through his governors

stages.name: Persian vassal
stages.desc: Own kings and fleets, under Persia: Phoenician cities, Cyprus, Cyrenaica

stages.name: Egyptian (Saite) kingdom
stages.desc: Egypt of the 26th dynasty, ruled from Sais, and its dependencies

stages.name: Carthaginian sphere
stages.desc: Carthage, Tyre's greatest colony, and the western Phoenicians

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The kings of Cyprus pay tribute to Amasis of Egypt
The Cypriot kings go over to Persia and add their ships to its fleet

states.name: Israel
timeline: Persian province 'Beyond the River'; Phoenician towns line the coast
Cedar from Lebanon is landed at Joppa for Jerusalem's temple

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Persian rule replaces Babylon's in Judah and around Gaza
Cyrus allows exiles to return to Jerusalem
Cambyses' army gathers at Gaza; Arab allies supply water for the desert crossing

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos, once Babylon's vassals, submit to Cyrus and keep their kings
Sidonians and Tyrians float cedar to Joppa for the temple in Jerusalem
The Phoenician fleet carries Cambyses' invasion of Egypt
Herodotus: the Phoenicians refuse to sail against Carthage, their own 'children'

states.name: Syria
timeline: Babylon's lands west of the Euphrates pass to Cyrus; Arwad keeps its own king
Cambyses dies in Syria on his way home, as revolt breaks out in Persia

states.name: Libya
timeline: Greek Cyrene and Barca in the east, Libyan peoples inland, Phoenician ports in the west
Arcesilaus III becomes king of Cyrene
The Libyans, Cyrene and Barca submit to Cambyses and send tribute

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage leads the western Phoenicians and honours Melqart of Tyre
Without the Phoenician fleet, Cambyses cannot reach Carthage

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Amasis rules a rich, independent Egypt from Sais
Amasis dies; his son Psamtik III inherits the coming war
Pelusium is lost and Memphis falls; Egypt becomes a Persian province
Cambyses buries the Apis bull with royal honours at Saqqara
Cambyses leaves Egypt; a rebel pharaoh, Petubastis, holds the western oases

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Salamis and the northern kingdoms pay tribute to Amasis
Salamis and its neighbours go over to Persia

events.title: Babylon falls
events.text: In October Cyrus' army enters Babylon, and the lands west of the Euphrates pass to Persia.

events.title: Cyrus Cylinder
events.text: Cyrus presents himself on a clay cylinder as Babylon's chosen king and restorer of its gods.

events.title: Tyre submits
events.text: Tyre, ruled by Hiram III according to Josephus, accepts Persian rule without a fight.

events.title: Sidon submits
events.text: Sidon, the other great Phoenician port, keeps its kings and its fleet under Persia.

events.title: Byblos
events.text: The old city of Byblos joins its neighbours in submitting to the Persians.

events.title: Arwad
events.text: The island city of Arwad, the northernmost Phoenician kingdom, accepts Persian rule.

events.title: Amasis of Egypt
events.text: Pharaoh Amasis rules a prosperous Egypt from Sais, allied to Greek states.

events.title: Naucratis
events.text: Amasis grants Greek merchants this Nile Delta port as their trading base in Egypt.

events.title: Cyprus under Egypt
events.text: Herodotus says Amasis was the first to conquer Cyprus and make it pay tribute.

events.title: Carthage
events.text: Founded by Tyre, by tradition in 814 BC, Carthage now leads the western Phoenicians.

events.title: Tithe to Melqart
events.text: By custom Carthage sends a tenth of its revenue to the temple of Melqart at Tyre.

events.title: Motya
events.text: This island town in western Sicily is a Phoenician outpost within Carthage's orbit.

events.title: Lepcis
events.text: Phoenician ports such as Lepcis trade along the coast of Tripolitania.

events.title: Return to Jerusalem
events.text: Cyrus allows exiles from Babylon to go home and rebuild Jerusalem's temple.

events.title: Cedar for the temple
events.text: The Book of Ezra says Sidonians and Tyrians brought cedar from Lebanon by sea to Joppa.

events.title: Polycrates of Samos
events.text: The tyrant Polycrates takes Samos, builds a war fleet and allies with Amasis.

events.title: Cambyses king
events.text: Cyrus dies fighting in Central Asia; his son Cambyses inherits the empire.

events.title: Arcesilaus III
events.text: A new king takes the throne of Cyrene, a Greek city long allied to Egypt.

events.title: Amasis dies
events.text: After forty-four years on the throne, Amasis dies and his son Psamtik III succeeds.

events.title: Phanes defects
events.text: Amasis' Greek mercenary captain Phanes flees to Cambyses with Egypt's secrets.

events.title: Cyprus changes sides
events.text: The kings of Cyprus abandon Egypt and join Persia, bringing their ships.

events.title: The fleet sails
events.text: Phoenician, Cypriot and Ionian Greek warships sail south with the Persian army.

events.title: Water in the desert
events.text: An Arab king's camels carry water for the army across northern Sinai.

events.title: Samian ships turn back
events.text: Polycrates sends forty warships to help Persia, but their crews turn back.

events.title: Battle of Pelusium
events.text: Cambyses defeats Psamtik III at Egypt's eastern gate; Herodotus saw the bones decades later.

events.title: Memphis falls
events.text: The Egyptians kill a Persian herald; after a siege, Memphis surrenders.

events.title: Udjahorresnet
events.text: Amasis' admiral serves Cambyses, shapes his pharaoh's titles and protects the temple of Neith at Sais.

events.title: Libyans submit
events.text: Fearing Egypt's fate, the Libyan peoples west of the Nile send gifts and tribute.

events.title: Cyrene and Barca
events.text: The Greek cities submit; Cambyses scorns Cyrene's small gift and scatters it to his troops.

events.title: Three campaigns
events.text: Cambyses plans to strike Carthage by sea, the Ammonians at Siwa and Kush in the south.

events.title: The fleet refuses
events.text: Herodotus: the Phoenicians, bound by oaths, will not sail against their own children.

events.title: Carthage spared
events.text: Without the Phoenician ships the fleet is too weak; Carthage is never attacked.

events.title: March to Ammon
events.text: Herodotus says fifty thousand men set out from Thebes against the oracle of Amun.

events.title: Kharga oasis
events.text: The army reaches the oasis Herodotus calls the Islands of the Blessed.

events.title: Lost in the sand
events.text: Herodotus: a south wind buried the whole army somewhere in the Western Desert.

events.title: Oracle of Amun
events.text: The army never reaches Siwa, the oracle Alexander would visit two centuries later.

events.title: March on Kush
events.text: Cambyses' march south fails for want of supplies, Herodotus says; Persia later claims Kush.

events.title: Apis buried
events.text: A stela from the Serapeum shows Cambyses honouring the Apis bull, not killing it.

events.title: Petubastis' revolt
events.text: Temple blocks from Dakhla name a rebel pharaoh; one scholar thinks he defeated the lost army.

events.title: Cambyses dies
events.text: Leaving Egypt to face a revolt in Persia, Cambyses dies of a wounded thigh in Syria.

chartNote: Share of the area of nine present-day countries, by the power that held most of each. Regions are today's boundaries, a simplification: Libya mixes Greek Cyrene, Libyan peoples and Phoenician ports, and Persia ruled the coasts and oases rather than the open desert. Egypt's vast area swings the shares.
